data.hypothesis: Baseline T3 measurements put the original decoder at 49.623 µs and predicate aggregation at 49.545 µs, while the measured shared-loop and table-DFA variants were slower. This distinct pure-scalar test replaces per-width validation branches in the main loop with masked predicates and arithmetic width advancement, using a bounded four-byte lookahead and the scalar decoder for the final short tail. It may reduce control-flow dependencies, but redundant lookahead loads for short sequences may erase any gain; the controller must measure it on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload.

memory_lessons.applicability: This candidate avoids both table lookups and a dynamic continuation loop, but adds safe redundant lookahead loads; measure rather than infer performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured table-DFA and shared-continuation-loop variants were slower than baseline, while bitwise predicate aggregation was close to baseline; these observations do not establish which mechanism caused the differences.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this masked-lookahead scalar variant against baseline and predicate aggregation with the same official mixed-width protocol.

memory_lessons.applicability: The main loop uses masked validity checks, while a separate short-tail decoder preserves bounded reads and explicit UTF-8 boundary checks.
memory_lessons.claim: A prior DFA development attempt failed protected correctness checks; a later restricted-class DFA was valid but measured slower. Compact-state changes therefore need official correctness validation as well as timing.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check official ASCII and malformed-input cases alongside all other required correctness cases before interpreting timing.

data.notes: Pure-scalar experiment; no hardware-specific instructions, threading changes, or contract changes. The main loop reads its four-byte lookahead only when at least four bytes remain, and the tail decoder handles shorter remainders. Previous observations include a failed DFA development variant (e87168de8c614fc4-h01); the current candidate has no controller correctness or timing result yet.
transformations: Keep the scalar ASCII-run skip and the existing run ABI and output assignment.
For non-ASCII bytes with at least four bytes remaining, use bounded lookahead loads and bitwise-masked continuation and UTF-8 boundary predicates instead of width-specific validation branches.
Advance by an arithmetically derived sequence width and use an explicit bounds-checked scalar decoder for the short tail.
